name: PMSA003I particulate matter sensor (I2C)
description: Plantower laser-scattering dust sensor with an I2C interface (address 0x12, fixed): reports PM1.0, PM2.5 and PM10 mass concentration (ug/m3, 0-500 effective range, 1 ug/m3 resolution) and particle counts per 0.1 L, refreshed about once per second. The breakout has a 5 V charge pump for the fan, a 3.3 V regulator and BSS138 level shifters, so it runs from 3-5 V. Sold as: Adafruit PMSA003I Air Quality Breakout - STEMMA QT / Qwiic (product 4632), 7-pin header VIN, 3Vo, GND, SCL, SDA, RST, SET plus two STEMMA QT connectors.
eli5: A tiny fan pulls air past a laser and counts the dust and smoke specks, telling your board over two wires how dirty the air is.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply, 3-5 V. Use the same voltage as your board's logic (3.3 V for ESP32/Pico): SDA/SCL are pulled up to VIN. An onboard charge pump makes the fan's 5 V.

pins.name: 3Vo
pins.description: 3.3 V output of the onboard regulator; not a supply input, leave unconnected

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock, level shifted; 10 kOhm pull-up to VIN on the board

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data, level shifted; 10 kOhm pull-up to VIN on the board

pins.name: RST
pins.description: Sensor reset, pull low to reset (diode-isolated, pulled up on the board); leave unconnected

pins.name: SET
pins.description: Sleep control: low = sleep (fan off), open/high = run (diode-isolated, pulled up on the board); leave unconnected

buildNotes: Power VIN from the same voltage as the microcontroller's logic (3V3 on an ESP32 or Pico): the board's 10 kOhm I2C pull-ups go to VIN, and the onboard charge pump still gives the fan its 5 V.
From 3.3 V the charge pump draws roughly twice the sensor's 100 mA, so feed it from a board whose 3.3 V regulator can spare about 200 mA.
I2C address 0x12 (cannot be changed), standard mode 100 kHz. Read 32 bytes starting at register 0x00.
Frame: 0x42 0x4D, frame length 28, 13 big-endian 16-bit words, then a 16-bit check code = sum of the first 30 bytes. Drop frames whose header, length or sum is wrong.
Use the 'atmospheric environment' values (words 4-6) for room or outdoor air; the CF=1 values (words 1-3) are meant for factory calibration.
Give it a few seconds after power-up before the first read, and about 30 s (fan spin-up) before trusting the numbers. Mount it with the inlet and outlet unobstructed, at least 20 cm above the floor.
Leave RST and SET unconnected for normal use; pulling SET low puts the sensor to sleep.

driver.code:
# Plantower PMSA003I laser particulate sensor (I2C version), MicroPython driver.
# From the PMSA003I data manual V2.6: I2C address 0x12, 100 kHz, "standard NXP EEPROM protocol".
# Registers 0x00-0x1F hold one 32-byte frame: 0x42 0x4D, frame length (2x13+2 = 28),
# 13 big-endian 16-bit data words, then a 16-bit check code = sum of bytes 0x00-0x1D.
# The sensor refreshes the frame about once per second.


class PMSA003I:
    ADDR = 0x12

    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=ADDR):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr

    def read(self):
        """Read one frame and return a dict of readings.
        Keys: pm1_0_cf1, pm2_5_cf1, pm10_cf1 (ug/m3, CF=1 'factory' values),
        pm1_0, pm2_5, pm10 (ug/m3, atmospheric environment: use these indoors/outdoors),
        n0_3, n0_5, n1_0, n2_5, n5_0, n10 (particles larger than that many um per 0.1 L of air),
        version, error.
        Raises ValueError on a bad header, length or checksum (e.g. still starting up)."""
        d = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, 0x00, 32)
        if d[0] != 0x42 or d[1] != 0x4D:
            raise ValueError('PMSA003I: bad frame header')
        if ((d[2] << 8) | d[3]) != 28:
            raise ValueError('PMSA003I: bad frame length')
        if (sum(d[0:30]) & 0xFFFF) != ((d[30] << 8) | d[31]):
            raise ValueError('PMSA003I: checksum mismatch')
        w = [(d[4 + 2 * i] << 8) | d[5 + 2 * i] for i in range(12)]
        return {
            'pm1_0_cf1': w[0], 'pm2_5_cf1': w[1], 'pm10_cf1': w[2],
            'pm1_0': w[3], 'pm2_5': w[4], 'pm10': w[5],
            'n0_3': w[6], 'n0_5': w[7], 'n1_0': w[8],
            'n2_5': w[9], 'n5_0': w[10], 'n10': w[11],
            'version': d[28], 'error': d[29],
        }

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from pmsa003i import PMSA003I

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=100000)
sensor = PMSA003I(i2c)
while True:
    try:
        r = sensor.read()
        print('PM1=%d PM2.5=%d PM10=%d ug/m3' % (r['pm1_0'], r['pm2_5'], r['pm10']))
    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
        print('waiting for sensor:', e)
    time.sleep(1)
